newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia, Malaysia postpone talks on islands.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia, Malaysia postpone talks on islands.

text.p: Indonesia and Malaysia agreed on Thursday to postpone talks on an island territorial dispute pending a ruling from the International Court of Justice (ICJ), the official Antara news agency reported.

Antara said Indonesia and Malaysia decided at the sixth ministerial meeting of the Indonesian-Malaysian Joint Commission, which was attended by the two countries' foreign ministers, to delay the talks until the ICJ issued its ruling.

Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said negotiations on the Sipadan-Ligitan issue have reached a stage where the two countries have agreed to wait for their governments to ratify a special agreement on the dispute, said Antara.
Both countries claim the islands of Sipadan and Ligitan in the Celebes Sea off Borneo and have at times backed their claims with a show of naval force.
Last October, the two countries announced they would submit the long-standing sovereignty dispute to the court, the main U.N. judicial body in The Hague.

Alatas said the special agreement still needed to be ratified by the two governments, adding that after the ratification, Indonesia and Malaysia would have to determine a convenient date to submit the dispute to the court.
The agency gave no further details.
